description: Ancestry of the cruciferous vegetables as a graph. Every node is a clade, a species, a crop lineage (a branch of cultivated forms inside a species) or a vegetable; every edge points from ancestor to descendant. Edge types: `descent` (branching between clades and species, from the Open Tree of Life), `hybrid-parent` (a species formed by two parent species combining genomes: the Triangle of U and ×Raphanobrassica), `domestication` (a cultivated branch inside a species), `selection` (a crop selected from that branch) and `cross` (a crop bred from two crops). Hybrids and crosses have two parents, so this is a network, not a single tree. Each vegetable has `lineage`: every path from the family root to it, written out. `confidence` marks how settled a step is: established, likely or debated. Genomes: A = B. rapa, B = black mustard, C = B. oleracea, R = radish. Every node also has `genome`: `state` (its chromosome make-up: karyotype, genome letters, 2n, ploidy), `change` (what changed on the branch into it, with confidence), `events` (all changes inherited from the family root, through both parents for hybrids) and `signature` (a compact code of the path; unique for each vegetable). Genome letters: A = B. rapa, B = black mustard, C = B. oleracea, R = radish. ACK = Ancestral Crucifer Karyotype (n = 8); PCK = Proto-Calepineae Karyotype (n = 7); WGT = whole-genome triplication of tribe Brassiceae.
